runs-lint.subsystem: Runs, budgets, lint, escalation, quality and config (hyperresearch HEAD 327498b)
runs-lint.summary:
This subsystem keeps a per-run manifest (research/runs/<tag>/run.json) plus an event log. The orchestrator records each step with `hpr run step`, and `run resume` computes the next step from the tier that step 1 declared. Around that sit a USD budget, opt-in source and note ceilings, the ship gate `run finish` (verify_run), an advisory lint battery of 26 declared rules, a SQLite queue that hands blocked URLs to a Chrome-driving agent (Claude Code only), a composite source-quality score, per-run posture shims ("levers"), profile gears whose numbers are rendered into prompts at install, a repair command, and the vault config.

Only verify_run binds. It checks that the report exists, a ±20% word band, headings by substring, a citation-density floor, one scaffold header, quote-integrity and retracted-citations, that tier artifact files exist, and that a cite-check patch log exists.

Everything else is prompt-level, opt-in or dead. The budget is never fed and `run resume` clears it. The ceilings fire only at step boundaries. Only word targets and the citation floor are read by code. Several lint rules are vacuous in the 3.0 layout.

The best idea here is one binding gate with quote-integrity and bounded fix rounds that end honestly blocked. Its main holes: density counts the bibliography, critic outputs can be stubbed, and quotes are matched against agent-written notes.

mechanisms.name: Run manifest + event log
mechanisms.what: run.json holds profile_steps, per-step status, chapters, spend counters, budget and ceilings; events.jsonl is append-only. Writes go to a tmp file and are atomically renamed; there is no lock. init is idempotent: an existing manifest comes back unchanged.
mechanisms.why: It is bookkeeping for recovery and telemetry; nothing in it touches report content.
mechanisms.cost: About 2 CLI calls per step (~32-40 per full run). Each `run step done` does ~4 manifest saves and 2 event appends. `run step -j` echoes the whole steps dict (run_cmd.py:345-346), roughly 0.5K tokens per call late in a run (estimate).

mechanisms.name: Resume position and Codex stop gate
mechanisms.what: resume_position returns the first profile step not done or skipped, plus chapters_pending, narrowed to the tier in prompt-decomposition.json. `run resume` flips paused, blocked or failed runs to running and returns the skill or step file to load. The Codex Stop hook blocks ending once while the newest run is running, was touched in the last 6 h, and has a next step.
mechanisms.why: It keeps long runs from dying or restarting mid-pipeline, especially on Codex. It does not raise content quality, and it gives wrong positions for sub-steps and chapters.
mechanisms.cost: One CLI call per recovery; one hook call per Stop attempt.

mechanisms.name: USD budget governor
mechanisms.what: add_spend accumulates the agent-reported estimated_usd and flips the run to blocked(budget) when it crosses budget_usd. `run status` reports budget_remaining_usd.
mechanisms.why: No skill or agent calls `run spend`, and the repo has no unit prices (runs.py:404), so it never trips. `run resume` clears it anyway.
mechanisms.cost: Zero in practice.

mechanisms.name: Count ceilings (max_sources / max_notes)
mechanisms.what: At each `run step done`, counts are read from the DB (notes tagged with the vault_tag, distinct source URLs joined to them) and the run blocks when a ceiling is crossed. Up to 3 force-clears are allowed, each with a baseline so the block re-fires only when the count grows.
mechanisms.why: It is a cost guard, opt-in, and the entry skill never passes it. It only detects overshoot after a whole step.
mechanisms.cost: 2 SQL COUNT queries per step-done.

mechanisms.name: Ship gate: run finish / verify_run
mechanisms.what: This is the only path to status done. Checks: report exists, length within ±20% of the profile word target, required headings (substring), citation density ≥ 9 per 1000 words, no '## User Prompt (VERBATIM' leak, quote-integrity and retracted-citations run in-process, critic/patch/polish artifact files exist, and the cite-check patch log exists when there are criticals. Failure sets blocked(verify). The skill allows 3 fix rounds, then an honest blocked state.
mechanisms.why: Folding the content lints into one binding command stopped orchestrators from re-labeling failures as false positives (runs.py:778-782, the Bench Q62 lesson). The length band and density floor shape the report, though both are gameable.
mechanisms.cost: One CLI call per round. A failed round triggers fix work, for example a full synthesizer compression pass for over-length reports (skills/hyperresearch.md:276). Up to 3 rounds.

mechanisms.name: Quote-integrity check
mechanisms.what: Every quoted span of 5 or more words (straight or curly double quotes, body only) must match an FTS5 porter phrase query against any vault note body. Errors fail the gate. The prescribed fix is to drop the quotation marks or make the quote verbatim.
mechanisms.why: It removes fabricated verbatim quotes and pushes framing quotes out of quotation marks. It checks existence in any note, including agent-written interim notes, not in the cited source.
mechanisms.cost: One FTS query per quote. Negligible.

mechanisms.name: Retracted-citations check
mechanisms.what: A wikilink citation to a note with is_retracted=1 must have 'retract' within 200 characters, or the gate fails.
mechanisms.why: It blocks unacknowledged retracted sources, but only for wikilink style; numbered [N] reports are never checked.
mechanisms.cost: One query plus a regex pass. Negligible.

mechanisms.name: Advisory lint battery
mechanisms.what: 26 declared rules: vault hygiene, workflow artifacts, locus coverage, patch-surgery, instruction coverage by substring, citation-style presence, provenance tree, extract coverage, numeric consistency (warnings), audit-gate. Lint never exits non-zero. The polish step runs 4 rules as pre-checks.
mechanisms.why: Only the 4 polish pre-checks feed agent action. Several rules are dead or vacuous in the 3.0 layout (audit-gate, scaffold-prompt, duplicate-ids, stale-indexes), and the rest look at whichever run or report is newest.
mechanisms.cost: Each call does auto_sync plus many whole-table queries. numeric-consistency builds an in-memory blob of all claims and source bodies (O(vault)). About 4 calls per run.

mechanisms.name: Browser-lane escalation queue
mechanisms.what: Blocked fetches go into a SQLite queue when the lane is enabled, utility ≥ 8.0 (unscored passes) and the run has fewer than 25 items. Claims are atomic (UPDATE ... RETURNING). `escalation ingest` writes the agent-supplied page text as a draft source note plus a sources row. CAPTCHA, 2FA and login go to needs_human, consolidated into one message to the user.
mechanisms.why: It recovers paywalled or bot-blocked sources on Claude Code with Claude-in-Chrome. Codex has no drainer, and the ingested text is LLM-transcribed.
mechanisms.cost: Serial browsing by one browser-fetcher, 10 items per drain (hard-coded in the skill), up to 25 per run. High wall time and tokens per page.

mechanisms.name: Composite quality score
mechanisms.what: A renormalized weighted mean of tier weight (0.35), utility/18 (0.20), authority percentile (0.25) and vault PageRank (0.20), with retracted sources floored at 0.05. `search --ranked` multiplies BM25 relevance by 0.5 + q. Step 10 uses it to build must-read lists; claims are sorted by it.
mechanisms.why: It orders which sources drafters read. But its inputs are LLM priors (tier labels, utility guessed before reading) plus link popularity, and it is recomputed only at step 2.7.
mechanisms.cost: Cheap SQL. It is recomputed by `graph rank`, `repair` and scholar enrich.

mechanisms.name: Levers / posture shims
mechanisms.what: Step 1 sets register (teach/survey/analyze/advocate), inference_depth (surface/standard/deep) and domain_notes. render_shims writes 4 role files (research, drafting, critics, polish) that the orchestrator must paste verbatim into spawn prompts. verify_run checks only that the files exist.
mechanisms.why: It fits drafting and critique to the genre (for example, critics do not flag hedging in teach or survey; a steel-man is mandatory in advocate). Pasting is instruction only.
mechanisms.cost: About 100-250 words per shim on every spawn, across roughly 40+ spawns in a full run (estimate).

mechanisms.name: Profiles / gears
mechanisms.what: Built-in profiles light, full, premier and dissertation define sources, fan-out, drafts, claims, critic caps, word targets, citation floor and time estimate. `profile use` persists the gear and re-renders the installed prompts. Only word_targets and citation_density_min are read by code.
mechanisms.why: Breadth (15-25 / 55-80 / 100-130 / 300-450 sources, 1 vs 3 drafts, critics on or off) is the main quality-and-cost lever, but it works only through prompt compliance.
mechanisms.cost: The main cost driver: ~30-40 min (light), ~1.5-2.5 h (full), ~3-5 h (premier), ~4-8 h (dissertation), per profiles.py:306, 324, 373, 414.

mechanisms.name: Repair
mechanisms.what: Force-syncs; stubs broken wikilinks into research/temp; auto-tags and auto-summarizes; promotes draft to review to evergreen by word count and links; rebuilds indexes; recomputes centrality and quality; updates agent docs.
mechanisms.why: Promotion gives a 1.5x search boost (config.py:225, fts.py:173-174) on structural grounds only, and stubs make fabricated wikilink targets resolve. Little positive effect on report content.
mechanisms.cost: A full vault rewrite pass, O(notes).

mechanisms.name: Vault config knobs
mechanisms.what: Covers fetch timeouts and size caps, junk and login-wall gates, the chrome lane, ranking weights, lint thresholds (extract 150 words, divisor 3), embeddings (off), and scholar OA recovery (full text ≥ 6000 characters; rescue_blocked builds notes from OA copies).
mechanisms.why: OA recovery and the junk gates change what text reaches notes; the ranking weights change curation. Several knobs are dead: exclude_patterns, drain_batch_size, scholar_enabled, index_pages, default_status.
mechanisms.cost: None by itself.

mechanisms.name: Stall detection and run report telemetry
mechanisms.what: possibly_stalled is set when the manifest is untouched for 30 minutes. `run report` gives per-step wall time, spend counters and event counts, per run or aggregated.
mechanisms.why: It reports on runs. The cost fields (agents_spawned, estimated_usd) are always 0 because nothing feeds them.
mechanisms.cost: Negligible.

weaknesses.evidence: run_cmd.py:48 'Hard ceiling on estimated API-equivalent spend'; runs.py:404 'this repo does not carry unit prices'; runs.py:294 'Agents rarely call `hpr run spend`'. The skill claims 'the queue drains on the next `hpr run resume`', but resume only flips status (run_cmd.py:203-208).

A grep finds no Python consumer of draft_count, claims_min, claims_cap, depth_budget_total, gap_fetch_cap, wave_done_ratio or vault_check_interval_s. Ceilings are opt-in and not passed by the entry skill (skills/hyperresearch.md:127).

weaknesses.evidence: runs.py:620/681/829 read with utf-8-sig, but levers.py:271/282 and lint.py:331/1013/1209/1265/1322/1410 use utf-8 and catch only (JSONDecodeError, OSError). lint.py:1293 itself advises `echo '{...}' > research/patch-log.json`, which writes UTF-16 in Windows PowerShell 5.1.

ideas_for_vafer: Adopt: one binding final verification step whose verdict the orchestrator may not re-litigate or re-run piecemeal (runs.py:778-782 Bench Q62 lesson).
Adopt: cap fix rounds at 2-3, then deliver with the failed checks disclosed in the report rather than a silent pass (skills/hyperresearch.md:281).
Adopt as a writing rule: quotation marks only for verbatim source text; a quote that cannot be verified loses its marks or gets corrected.
Adapt: verify each quoted span and headline number against the notes entry for the same cited URL (VAFER notes already store URL + a verbatim quote of at most 30 words), not against any note.
Adapt: count and check citations in the body only, and require every [n] to resolve to a listed source that was opened; never let the bibliography satisfy a density check.
Avoid: self-reported spend or budget counters; agents skip bookkeeping. Cap cost structurally (researcher counts, waves), as VAFER tiers already do.
Avoid: existence-only checks for review stages; if VAFER adds a critic, its output must quote the report spans it judged, or the method note must not claim the stage ran.
Avoid: word-count bands as a ship gate; they trigger forced compression or expansion passes. Keep proportional effort.
Adapt: keep run state in plan.md checklist rows; if work is split by section, key progress by (section, phase), never by phase alone.
Adopt: list unreachable or blocked URLs once, with reasons, in the 'Not established' or access-gaps section so the user can fetch them.
Adapt: a one-line register (teach/survey/analyze/advocate) and inference depth (surface/standard/deep) in plan.md, read by the writing step and any critic; cheap genre control.
Avoid: numeric composite source-quality scores built from LLM priors and link popularity; keep VAFER's primary-record-first rule.
Avoid: 'newest file wins' lookups across runs; always address the current run folder explicitly.
Adopt for any VAFER helper script: read with utf-8-sig, catch UnicodeDecodeError, and tell agents in hosts.md not to write files with Windows PowerShell 5.1 '>' redirection (UTF-16).
Avoid: accumulating dead or legacy checks; every VAFER check should have a test that fails when its input is missing.
Adapt: if VAFER cites papers, check the retraction status of every cited DOI regardless of citation style.

key_claims.claim: The only binding quality gate is `run finish` (verify_run), the sole path to status done. It folds just two content rules (quote-integrity, retracted-citations) in-process because orchestrators re-interpreted separately run lint failures as false positives. All other lint rules are advisory, and `hpr lint` never exits non-zero.

The USD budget is non-functional in the shipped pipeline. estimated_usd changes only via `hpr run spend --usd`, the repo has no unit prices, no skill or agent prompt calls `run spend`, and `run resume` clears a budget block to running anyway (asserted by a test).
key_claims.where: core/runs.py:301-324, 404; cli/run_cmd.py:48, 203-208; tests/test_core/test_runs.py:344-355; grep of skills/ and core/hooks.py for 'run spend' returns nothing

key_claims.claim: Cost and breadth are governed by prompt text, not code. Profile numbers are rendered into prompts at install, and only word_targets and citation_density_min are read by Python at run time. Count ceilings are opt-in, checked only at step-done, and never passed by the entry skill.
The citation-density floor counts bibliography '[N]' entries and any '[[...]]' whether or not it resolves, because the regex runs over the full report text rather than the body.

The critic stage is not enforced. verify_run checks only that the critic-findings and patch-log files exist, and the polish skill tells the orchestrator to write '{"findings":[]}' stubs when a critic fails twice.
Quote-integrity verifies that a quote exists anywhere in the vault FTS index, which includes agent-written interim, extract and temp notes, not that it appears in the cited source.

enforcement.subsystem: Hooks, ship gate, stop gate, tool locks and installation
enforcement.summary:
This subsystem installs hyperresearch and provides every code-level control over a run. For Claude Code it installs a CLAUDE.md block (about 3.1K tokens, always loaded), an entry router skill, 18 step skills, 16 subagents whose `tools:` lines are the tool locks, and a PreToolUse hook that only adds a reminder on WebSearch/WebFetch. For Codex it installs AGENTS.md, the router skill, 18 plain step files, 15 TOML agents (where the locks become prose) and a Stop hook that runs `run stop-gate`. The ship gate (`run finish`, which calls `verify_run`) is the only way a run reaches status done. It checks length within ±20%, headings by substring, citation density, quote-integrity, retractions, and that the critic/patch/polish files exist.

Enforcement is weaker than the README claims. Claude Code has no Stop hook, so calling the gate is voluntary. The gate never checks step completion, and its artifact checks pass on stub files the orchestrator writes itself. The Codex gate trusts self-reported steps, can force a continuation at most once per stop chain, and is off in default `codex exec`. Only the patcher and polish Read+Edit locks really protect report quality. Windows bugs: settings.json is overwritten when it starts with a BOM, the corpus-critic gets a backslash path, CLI paths are unquoted, and prompts use POSIX syntax under PowerShell. Notes: C:/Users/VECTOR/Documents/GitHub/VAFER/docs/research/2026-10-27-hyperresearch/read-enforcement.md

mechanisms.name: Ship gate (run finish / verify_run)
mechanisms.what: Runs a battery of checks: report exists, length within ±20% of the profile target, required headings (substring), citation density of at least 9 per 1000 words, one scaffold-header leak check, quote-integrity, retracted-citations, critic/patch/polish artifacts exist, cite-check resolved if step 14.5 is marked done, shim files present. Flips the manifest to done or blocked(verify). It is the only path to 'done'.
mechanisms.why: The length and quote checks target the two failures actually seen: a 25,647-word report against a 16K ceiling, and 24 hallucinated quotes waved off as 'false positives' (CHANGELOG.md:203). The length band encodes their benchmark finding that 45-55KB reports score best (hooks.py:991-994). Most other checks are structural or existence-only, and nothing forces the gate to be called on Claude Code.
mechanisms.cost: One local CLI call (seconds), then up to 3 fix rounds. The length remedy re-spawns the synthesizer for a full compression rewrite, the most expensive single fix.

mechanisms.name: Quote-integrity content check (folded into gate)
mechanisms.what: Every double-quoted span of 5 or more words in the report body must phrase-match some vault note via FTS. Error severity, so it blocks.
mechanisms.why: Blocks verbatim fabricated quotes. But the match is vault-wide, including LLM-written interim and source-analysis notes, and a report with frontmatter is indexed and matches itself. Single and CJK quotes are ignored. Its prescribed fix is 'drop the quotation marks', so it polices quote hygiene, not claim support.
mechanisms.cost: One FTS query per quoted span; negligible.

mechanisms.name: Upstream length gate plus synthesizer compression respawn
mechanisms.what: After synthesis the orchestrator counts words mechanically. If the report is over the ceiling, the synthesizer is re-spawned once to compress. The ship gate later fails anything more than 20% over the high end.
mechanisms.why: Keeps reports in the length band their RACE data favours. The synthesizer has no Bash and cannot count words, so the check falls to the orchestrator.
mechanisms.cost: A word-count call; a compression respawn is a full rewrite by an opus-class agent (tens of thousands of tokens).

mechanisms.name: Citation-density floor
mechanisms.what: Counts [N], [N, M] and wikilinks across the whole report text against a floor of 9 per 1000 words (characters/3 for scripts without word boundaries).
mechanisms.why: Forces dense citation, which their scoring rewards. But the bibliography's own [N] lines count, and markers are never resolved to sources.
mechanisms.cost: Negligible.

mechanisms.name: Tier-artifact and cite-check existence checks
mechanisms.what: Full tier requires the four critic-findings files, patch-log.json and polish-log.json to exist. Cite-check findings (plus a patch log if any finding is critical) are required only when step 14.5 is marked done.
mechanisms.why: Existence only. The orchestrator pre-stubs patch-log and polish-log before the agents run (14-patcher.md:53-59, 15-polish.md:34), and leaving 14.5 unmarked skips its check.
mechanisms.cost: Negligible.

mechanisms.name: Codex Stop hook (stop gate)
mechanisms.what: .codex/hooks.json runs `hyperresearch run stop-gate`. It prints a block decision while the newest run is 'running', was touched within 6 hours, and still has a next step in its manifest.
mechanisms.why: Pushes Codex back into the pipeline once a run has started; Codex's documented failure is answering inline. But it trusts self-reported steps, goes silent once all steps are marked done/skipped or the run is blocked (including a failed gate), cannot fire without `run init`, forces at most one continuation per stop chain, and does not run under default `codex exec`.
mechanisms.cost: One Python CLI start per stop attempt (about a second). Zero tokens unless it blocks, then about 60 tokens of reason.

mechanisms.name: Claude PreToolUse reminder hook
mechanisms.what: A node script on WebSearch|WebFetch that injects a 703-character 'check the vault first, use hyperresearch fetch' reminder as additionalContext. Always exits 0 and never denies.
mechanisms.why: Advisory only. Never installed for --global users. Its 'use subagents to fetch in parallel' advice cannot be followed inside fetchers, which have no Task tool.
mechanisms.cost: About 175 tokens plus one node process per web call, in the main session and in fetcher subagents.

mechanisms.name: Subagent tool allowlists (Claude Code tool locks)
mechanisms.what: `tools:` frontmatter per agent: patcher and polish auditor Read+Edit; synthesizer and readability recommender Read+Write; critics, cite-checker, loci analyst, corpus critic and source analyst Bash+Read+Write; fetcher adds WebSearch; depth-investigator adds Task; browser-fetcher adds ToolSearch.
mechanisms.why: Read+Edit genuinely stops the patch and polish passes from regenerating the synthesized report. The other locks do not prevent what the prompts claim: critics and the readability recommender hold Write, and critics hold Bash. The main orchestrator is never locked.
mechanisms.cost: No runtime cost.

mechanisms.name: Codex tool-discipline preamble and TOML translation
mechanisms.what: Turns each agent's tools line into prose rules ('Codex cannot enforce that list, so you must') plus a tool-vocabulary map. Every agent gets sandbox_mode workspace-write; reasoning effort is high for opus-class roles, medium otherwise.
mechanisms.why: Purely instructional. The effort mapping probably matters more than the rules.
mechanisms.cost: About 400-900 extra characters per agent prompt.

mechanisms.name: Fresh per-step procedure loading
mechanisms.what: The entry skill is a router. Each step's procedure is loaded only when that step runs, via the Skill tool on Claude or by reading .hyperresearch/codex/steps/*.md on Codex.
mechanisms.why: Their evidence: V7's single 1200-line skill was compacted away, and the orchestrator dropped steps and the triple draft 'in 100% of runs' where it did not re-read the skill. Q57 scored 55.9 with the full pipeline against Q9's 52.6 with a single draft.
mechanisms.cost: About 3.5K tokens per Claude session to list 19 skills (Codex avoids the listing). Roughly 190K characters of step templates across a full run.

mechanisms.name: Run manifest, run step and run resume
mechanisms.what: run.json per run holds step status, spend and chapters. `run resume` computes the next step from the tier declared in the decomposition.
mechanisms.why: Gives a recovery path that survives context compaction. But it is self-reported, 'skipped' counts as done, and resume silently clears budget and failed-gate blocks.
mechanisms.cost: About 2 CLI calls per step (about 34 per full run) plus a SQLite count reconcile at each 'done'.

mechanisms.name: Count ceilings and budget governor
mechanisms.what: Optional --max-sources/--max-notes ceilings checked at step done; --budget blocks the run when estimated_usd crosses it.
mechanisms.why: Not passed by default. The budget is inert because agents rarely call `run spend` (CHANGELOG.md:9), and `run resume` clears it.
mechanisms.cost: Negligible.

mechanisms.name: Agent docs injection (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md)
mechanisms.what: A marked section with the CLI path, how to start a run, run management, scholar search, the untrusted-content policy and the curation pass.
mechanisms.why: Orientation only; the skill files win on any conflict.
mechanisms.cost: About 3.1K tokens (CLAUDE.md) or 1K (AGENTS.md) in every session of the project, research or not.

mechanisms.name: Installer rendering, provenance, idempotency and pruning
mechanisms.what: Renders Jinja templates (<< >> delimiters) per profile and platform, stamps a provenance header, writes only changed files, and prunes retired or stale files that carry its markers.
mechanisms.why: Maintenance. Inconsistent .format/.replace handling leaves {{ }} in three installed agents and a raw Windows path in one.
mechanisms.cost: Install time only.

mechanisms.name: Global install, lazy steps-only bootstrap and plugin bootstrap skill
mechanisms.what: --global puts the entry skill and agents in ~/.claude (Claude) or in ~/.agents and ~/.codex (Codex). The first run in a project runs `init` and `install --steps-only`. The Claude and Codex plugins ship only a deep-research bootstrap skill that runs `install .` mid-session.
mechanisms.why: Distribution only. It adds mid-session install fragility, since agents load at session start.
mechanisms.cost: One or two CLI calls on the first run; possibly a session restart.

mechanisms.name: Pre-stubbed logs for Edit-only agents
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator writes empty patch-log.json and polish-log.json before spawning the Read+Edit agents, so they have a file they can Edit.
mechanisms.why: Plumbing forced by the lock. Side effect: the stubs satisfy the ship gate's existence checks before the agents have run.
mechanisms.cost: One shell call each.

mechanisms.name: Fail-safe escape hatches
mechanisms.what: HYPERRESEARCH_STOP_GATE=0, the stop_hook_active guard, fail-open on any exception, a 6-hour staleness window, and refusal to overwrite an unparseable hooks.json.
mechanisms.why: Prevents wedged sessions; the same hatches make the gate easy to bypass.
mechanisms.cost: None.

ideas_for_vafer: Adopt: make one gate command the only way to mark a run complete, record its verdict durably, allow at most 3 fix rounds, and forbid re-interpreting a failed check.
Adapt: install a Stop hook on Claude Code too, blocking until the gate has passed or the user explicitly aborted, not merely until the manifest shows no next step.

Adapt: keep the stop hook's safety features (env-var off switch, fail-open on exceptions, staleness window), but count nudges in run state instead of relying on stop_hook_active, so the gate can push more than once with a bounded cap.
Adopt: on both platforms, store step procedures as plain files read on demand (hyperresearch's Codex layout); this avoids the per-session skill-listing cost and any dependence on hot-reload.
Adopt: on Claude Code, make patch and polish agents Read+Edit only; it is the one lock that structurally prevents regenerating the report.
Avoid claiming locks that do not exist. Give critics no Write or Bash, and have the orchestrator write their findings from the returned message.
Adapt: check verbatim quotes against the cited source's fetched text only, excluding LLM-written notes and the report itself, and cover single, curly and CJK quote marks.

Adapt: replace existence checks with content checks: schema-valid findings, a patch log covering every finding, and a changed report hash when edits were applied. Make them impossible to satisfy with stubs.
Adapt: derive step completion from verified artifacts, not self-reported step calls, and fold skip detection (loci without investigations, missing reconciliation, skipped criticals) into the gate.
Adapt: compute citation density on the body only, require every [N] to resolve, and require every listed source to be cited.
Fix: run the retraction check for every citation style, not only wikilinks.
Avoid: never rewrite a user's settings file after a parse failure. Read with utf-8-sig and refuse to write on error.
Avoid baking an absolute unquoted CLI path into prompts; use one quoted, relocatable invocation such as `python -m vafer`.
Avoid POSIX-only syntax in prompts (`VAR=x cmd`, `echo > file`, bash loops); create stubs and run checks through the CLI so PowerShell hosts work.
Avoid a large always-loaded footprint: no multi-thousand-token CLAUDE.md block, and one entry skill instead of 19 listed skills.
Avoid recovery commands that silently clear budget or failed-gate blocks.
Adapt: use deny-with-reason hooks only for rules that matter (for example, blocking WebFetch of source pages during a run), and drop reminder-only hooks.
Adapt: ship agents with the plugin so they load at session start, or detect missing subagent types and stop with a restart instruction instead of improvising.
Adopt the per-run manifest and resume command for recovery after context compaction, but compute the manifest from the artifacts on disk.
Avoid hiding benchmark-tuned thresholds (length bands, density floors) in gates; tell the user what they optimise.

key_claims.claim: On Claude Code nothing structural makes a run finish or makes the orchestrator call the ship gate. The only Claude hook is a PreToolUse reminder on WebSearch|WebFetch that always exits 0 and injects additionalContext; the Stop hook is installed only for Codex.
key_claims.where: src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:3557-3604 (hook script), hooks.py:3815-3825 (matcher), hooks.py:3674-3688 (Stop hook only in the Codex branch); skills/hyperresearch.md:180; CHANGELOG.md:203

key_claims.claim: verify_run never checks manifest step completion (apart from the step 14.5 condition), and its tier-artifact checks are existence-only. patch-log.json and polish-log.json are pre-stubbed by the orchestrator before the patcher and polish agents run, so the gate passes even if those agents never ran. The skip-detecting lint rules (workflow, locus-coverage, patch-surgery) are error severity but are not part of the gate.

The Codex stop gate enforces only self-reported manifest progress. It is silent when no run exists (the inline-answer case it was built for), when every step is marked done or skipped even if run finish never ran, when the run is blocked (including a failed ship gate), whenever the hook input carries stop_hook_active (after it has already blocked once), and under default codex exec without --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust.

Only the patcher and polish-auditor locks (Read, Edit) structurally constrain report changes on Claude Code. Critics and the readability recommender hold Write (critics also hold Bash) even though their prompts say they cannot modify the report. The 'per-hunk caps' the README cites do not exist in code, and on Codex there are no locks at all.

Quote-integrity, the strongest content check in the gate, verifies only double-quoted spans of 5 or more words, using a vault-wide FTS phrase match that includes LLM-written interim and source-analysis notes. It never ties a quote to its cited source, and its prescribed fix is removing the quotation marks.

On Windows, `hyperresearch install` can silently replace a user's .claude/settings.json with a file containing only its hook. It reads with utf-8, falls back to {} on JSONDecodeError (for example, a UTF-8 BOM) and rewrites the file; the Codex installer refuses in the same situation.

claims-history.subsystem: Claims versus evidence: README, DRACO benchmark, CHANGELOG, 2.0 roadmap, Codex bench, tests and GitHub issues
claims-history.summary: This subsystem is hyperresearch's public evidence layer: the README's claims, a DRACO board the vendor ran itself, a candid CHANGELOG, a 2.0 roadmap written in the same commit that ticked it done, a Codex adherence bench, a Python-only test suite and 47 GitHub issues. Checked against the code and primary sources, the headline '#1 on DRACO' measures the hosted 'Hyperresearch Deep' path: chaptered research, a one-pass single writer and a figure-level claim check. The vendor's own docs say Deep uses the open-source 16-step writing chain (triple draft, four critics, patcher) only as a fallback. The lead over Claude Research rests on 10 tasks the vendor chose and calls easier, with a 5-5 per-task split. One medicine task supplies 75% of the gap (paired p~0.31). The comparators were handled unevenly, and 3 of hyperresearch's 10 reports were rewritten afterwards. The earlier 'leads DeepResearch-Bench' claim was a projection from a 9-query pilot. Several advertised enforcements are prose or inert: the budget cap, the per-hunk cap, a Claude Code stop gate, and 'every citation verified'. The CHANGELOG shows recurring failure classes: skipped prose gates, features that never worked, and constants authored twice. Tests cover the Python layer well but nothing an LLM does. mechanisms.name: DRACO self-benchmark (vendor-run 10-task subset)
mechanisms.what: Hyperresearch (HR) picked one task per DRACO domain plus one extra medicine task. It ran its hosted Deep product and the comparators: consumer apps for Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, and other vendors' published outputs for Valyu, Parallel and You.com. All were graded with the DRACO paper's per-criterion rubric grader under GPT-5.2 (reasoning off, temperature 0), with two grades averaged for most systems.
mechanisms.why: It is measurement and marketing, not a pipeline mechanism. n=10, a 5-5 per-task split against Claude Research, Medicine supplies 75% of the gap, exact paired p~0.31. It measures hosted Deep, not the OSS pipeline.
mechanisms.cost: 11 tasks x 8 systems x 1-2 grading passes. A hosted Deep run is $49 and 3-5 h each. Grading cost is not published.

mechanisms.name: Hosted Deep writing path (one-pass writer)
mechanisms.what: 3-5 research chapters; an evidence map built by reading every kept source in full; one report plan with per-section briefs saying which section owns which table and figure; a bounded, primary-first 'needs fetch' for plan gaps; one writer over the plan-ordered evidence; fallbacks (a second model, then section-by-section writers plus an editor); model-free repairs; a claim check of every cited figure with one guarded revision; a verification receipt.
mechanisms.where: https://hyperresearch.ai/how-it-works (updated 2026-10-02). Absent from the OSS src/: a grep for one-pass writer, evidence map, needs fetch and section-by-section returns nothing.
mechanisms.why: This path produced the DRACO numbers, and the vendor demoted the OSS critic chain to a fallback, so it is the vendor's revealed preference. No ablation is published.
mechanisms.cost: $49 per hosted run, 3-5 h, 150-200 sources (pricing page). Token use is unknown.

mechanisms.name: OSS 'older writing path' (triple draft, synthesizer, 4 critics, gap-fetch, patcher, cite-check, polish, readability)
mechanisms.what: Steps 10-16 of the open-source pipeline, mandatory for the full tier. Writing the report directly in step 10 is a 'PIPELINE VIOLATION'.
mechanisms.where: README.md:156-163; src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch.md:298-299; how-it-works page: 'The older writing path is the one the open-source CLI still runs'
mechanisms.why: No published ablation. The vendor uses it only as a fallback for its own best product, yet README 'Why it wins' (README.md:51-61) credits it for the DRACO result.
mechanisms.cost: About 10 Opus-class agent spawns per run (3 draft orchestrators, synthesizer, 4 critics, patcher, polish, readability) plus a Sonnet cite-checker. Full tier takes 1.5-2.5 h (README.md:172). One user reported about 8.6x a $25 budget (#92).

mechanisms.name: Mechanical ship gate (run finish / verify_run)
mechanisms.what: One command checks required headings, length within +/-20%, citation density of at least 9 per 1000 words, tier artifacts, scaffold leaks, cite-check criticals, quote-integrity and retracted citations. It flips the manifest to done or blocked, with a bounded 3-round fix loop.
mechanisms.why: It blocks fabricated quotes and over-length reports that prose gates let through (CHANGELOG.md:203). The checks are structural only. On Claude Code nothing forces the agent to call it (no Stop hook), and the skills' '$HPR run finish' failed with 'command not found' from 2026-07-20 to 2026-09-22 (CHANGELOG.md:27).
mechanisms.cost: Cheap Python, plus up to 3 fix rounds.

mechanisms.name: Cite-check step 14.5 (mechanical triage plus sampled LLM tier)
mechanisms.what: Extracts (sentence, citation) pairs. It auto-passes a pair when the sentence's numbers appear as substrings in the cited note's concatenated claims, or when it shares a 6-word shingle with them. All unmatched number-bearing pairs and 60% of the rest go to a Sonnet cite-checker, followed by a second patcher pass.
mechanisms.why: It catches dangling citations and some unsupported claims. But the numeric substring auto-pass certifies wrong-entity and wrong-metric sentences (#150), sampling leaves 40% of weak pairs unchecked, and it runs on the full tier only (README.md:161).
mechanisms.cost: Sonnet calls on the sampled pairs, scaling with citation count. The roadmap expects thousands of pairs at dissertation scale (phase-5-verification.md:91).

mechanisms.name: Quote-integrity lint
mechanisms.what: Every quoted span of 5 or more words must appear verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in some vault note. A miss blocks run finish.
mechanisms.why: It mechanically kills fabricated quotes; one premier run had 24 flagged (CHANGELOG.md:203). The scope is narrow: quoted text only.
mechanisms.cost: Cheap text and SQL matching.

mechanisms.name: Budget governor and count ceilings
mechanisms.what: run init --budget, --max-sources and --max-notes set ceilings that are checked at step boundaries and should block the run.
mechanisms.why: It is inert. No skill or agent prompt calls 'run spend' (grep count 0), and the entry skill calls run init without any ceiling (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch.md:124).
mechanisms.cost: It costs nothing to run, which is the problem: it gives no cost protection.

mechanisms.name: Lazy per-step skill loading
mechanisms.what: The router invokes one step skill per phase, so each procedure loads fresh into context and is not evicted by compaction.
mechanisms.why: It addresses a documented V7 failure: the triple draft was dropped 'in 100% of runs' where the orchestrator did not re-read the skill. It improves adherence, not quality. Conditional branches are still skipped silently (#38).
mechanisms.cost: 18 step files and one Skill call per step; adds complexity.

mechanisms.name: Benchmark wrapper contract
mechanisms.what: The harness writes research/prompt.txt and wrapper_contract.json, which force inline [N] citations, a Sources list with URLs, and a mandatory '## Opinionated Synthesis' section with 5 subsections.
mechanisms.why: Resolvable URLs are required by FACT and the DRACO citation criteria; before the fix, bench reports carried zero verifiable URLs. The synthesis block is benchmark packaging that normal users do not get.
mechanisms.cost: None.

mechanisms.name: Codex adherence bench
mechanisms.what: Each query runs in an isolated project via codex exec with workspace-write and network. It records vault notes, manifest steps, tier, spawns, sandbox rejections and run verify, flags inline answers as PIPELINE_SKIPPED, and exports RACE-format JSONL.
mechanisms.why: It measures whether the pipeline ran, not report quality. No results are published (gitignored), and README.md:460 says the Codex port 'has not been benchmarked yet'.
mechanisms.cost: One codex exec session per query, with a 3 h default timeout (codex_bench/harness.py:49).

mechanisms.name: Benchmark-driven prompt tuning (register levers, pedagogy primers, coverage-before-elegance)
mechanisms.what: Prompt changes derived from RACE comparisons on single DeepResearch-Bench queries such as Q62: a register lever, 3-5 sentence primers per section, and 'cut prose, never points'.
mechanisms.why: The changes are plausible coverage and pedagogy gains, but the evidence is one query against one judge ('+2.5 RACE from register alone', CHANGELOG.md:194).
mechanisms.cost: Prompt complexity and per-run shim rendering.

mechanisms.name: Golden-prompt and profile-field tests
mechanisms.what: Rendered skills and agents are pinned byte for byte, and a test asserts every Profile field is read outside profiles.py.
mechanisms.why: They prevent silent prompt drift and dead config (the field test found 8 dead fields), but say nothing about agent behaviour or report quality.
mechanisms.cost: Low; the goldens need maintenance.

ideas_for_vafer: Adopt the vendor's own best shape, not the OSS chain: a plan with per-section briefs, then a primary-first fetch for plan gaps, then one writer over all plan-ordered evidence, with section-by-section writing only as a fallback.
Avoid the triple-draft, 4-critic and patcher stack: the vendor demoted it to a fallback, and nothing shows it adds quality for its large Opus cost.
Require every conditional branch to leave a written verdict in plan.md, including skips ('source-analyst: none, because ...'); unlogged branches get dropped silently (#38).
Check each figure by entity, metric, unit and period against the opened page, never by matching number substrings, and recompute every derived ratio or percentage before shipping.
Extend the existing headline-fact re-check to every number in the summary, and run it in every tier that writes a report (HR's light tier gets no cite-check).
Always give resolvable URLs in Sources; DRACO citation criteria (12%) and FACT penalize missing links, and ChatGPT and Gemini lost points from export alone.

For medical, legal and financial tasks, add a safety rule (no prescriptive dosing or legal directives without caveats and an escalation path); DRACO penalties reach -500 and one medicine task decided HR's #1.
Take bibliography titles from page metadata (citation_title, og:title, Crossref, OpenAlex), never from the first PDF line; 39% of the titles in HR's sample report were junk.
Grep the final report for pipeline vocabulary ('corpus', 'in-corpus', 'notes', 'wave', 'locus') and rewrite those lines for the reader.
In the docs, separate what code enforces from what the model is only asked to do; never advertise a cap or gate that is just an instruction.

Before claiming to beat hyperresearch: use the full 100 DRACO tasks (at least 30), the same open-source rubric grader, at least 2 judge runs, paired per-task CIs or a sign test, an identical export path, and no post-hoc rewrites of our own reports.

For a like-for-like comparison with HR's board, grade with GPT-5.2 (reasoning off, temperature 0) on HR's same 10 tasks, also run Gemini-3-Pro on all 100 if it is available, and report Medicine separately.
Compete on cost and time: HR Deep is $49 and 3-5 h, while Perplexity DR scored 70.5 at about 245 s in the DRACO paper; aim for a Standard tier that finishes in minutes.
Treat 'answered without opening pages' as a hard failure (HR's April Codex run did exactly this), and put a pages-opened count in the method note.
Author each number once: the tier table should be the single source for the budgets other sections reference (HR's #101 found constants authored twice).
Do not use benchmark-only packaging (such as forced 'Opinionated Synthesis' sections) in eval runs unless users get the same output, or benchmark wins will not transfer.
Keep a candid CHANGELOG with failure post-mortems like HR's, its most useful artifact, and publish eval prompts, outputs and grades with any score claim.

pipeline-middle.subsystem: Depth, reconciliation, critique of the corpus, and drafting (hyperresearch steps 5-11)
pipeline-middle.summary: Full-tier only. Step 5 spawns up to six Sonnet depth investigators, one per locus that step 4 scored (four LLM-assigned 0-10 scores, bracketed source budgets). Each reads its seed notes, fetches up to its budget through nested fetcher subagents, and writes one interim note ending in a committed position with confidence, boundary conditions and what would change it. Step 6: the orchestrator reconciles those positions into 3-5 cross-locus tensions (comparisons.md). Step 7: it reads 8-12 full sources and records 3-7 expert disagreements with pre-committed resolutions. Step 8: a period-pinned filing check, one Sonnet corpus critic asking what would overturn each position, and 2-4 gap fetchers. Step 9: the orchestrator filters fetcher-written claims into an 80-120-item quote digest. Step 10: three Opus drafters, each with an angle (thesis, steelman-contrarian, reconciler) and a curated 20-50-note list read in full, write complete drafts. Step 11: the orchestrator source-checks cross-draft conflicts and writes a plan and outline; a fresh Read+Write Opus synthesizer rewrites everything in two passes. Drafts are rewritten, not chosen. The ship gate checks none of these steps. Full notes: C:/Users/VECTOR/Documents/GitHub/VAFER/docs/research/2026-10-27-hyperresearch/read-pipeline-middle.md

mechanisms.name: Scored locus selection with bracketed depth budgets (step 4 feeding step 5)
mechanisms.what: Two Sonnet loci analysts propose loci from note titles, summaries and the first ~400 characters, plus contradiction clusters. The orchestrator dedupes to at most 6, scores importance, uncertainty, disagreement and decision impact 0-10 each, sums them (max 40), and assigns 15/10/5/0-3 new sources by bracket. Step 5 spawns one investigator per locus with budget > 0, capped at 6. At least one dialectical locus is mandatory.
mechanisms.why: Concentrates depth on contested, decision-relevant questions and forces at least one disagreement into the report. But every score is an LLM judgment, loci are picked from summaries rather than full text, and the stated 40-source total is not enforced (the brackets allow 90).
mechanisms.cost: 2 Sonnet subagents plus orchestrator scoring. Small next to steps 5 and 10, but it sets the size of step 5 (up to 6 investigators).

mechanisms.name: Parallel depth investigators that must end in a calibrated committed position
mechanisms.what: One Sonnet subagent per locus reads its seed notes and claim files (targeting opposing stances on the same stance_target), fetches up to source_budget by spawning fetcher subagents through Task, and writes one interim note. Sections: corpus view, new sources, evidence synthesis (a steelman per side for dialectical loci), committed position with Position, Confidence (numeric bands), Boundary conditions, What would change this, Evidence weight, and a push for specific thresholds.
mechanisms.why: Gives later steps claims to reconcile rather than facts to assemble, adds targeted sources, and supplies the falsifiers steps 6 and 8 use. Every drafter reads every interim note in full. Caveat: on Claude Code the fetch path depends on nested Task spawning, which I could not verify works.
mechanisms.cost: Up to 6 Sonnet sessions (estimate 50-120K peak context each) plus nested fetchers (count unspecified). Nominally 40 new sources, more with each fetcher's mandatory 3-8-source chase. Dozens of tool calls per investigator.

mechanisms.name: Cross-locus reconciliation into comparisons.md
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator lays all committed positions side by side and asks five relationship questions of every pair: same facts with different meaning, conflicting evidence, hidden assumption, special case, convergence by different mechanisms. It keeps the 3-5 strongest and records each one's positions, dynamic, how the draft must engage it, and calibration weighting.
mechanisms.why: Builds the argumentative spine that the plan and drafts must engage, and turns shared falsifiers into flagged open questions. It is written by the orchestrator in a heavily loaded context, and nothing checks that the final report engages each tension.
mechanisms.cost: No subagent. All interim notes enter the main context a second time (estimate +20-40K tokens).

mechanisms.name: Source-tension extraction with pre-committed resolutions
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator surveys the 15-20 best sources and reads 8-12 full bodies, mines orphan contradiction clusters that never became loci, ranks candidates by decision relevance, evidence quality and reader value, and writes 3-7 tensions as JSON with both sides' evidence, proponent note ids and a committed resolution.
mechanisms.why: Catches disagreements that locus analysis misses and forces a verdict on each. The 'mandatory Source Tensions section' it promises has no downstream consumer contract, so its reach into the report depends on drafters and the synthesizer choosing to use it.
mechanisms.cost: Orchestrator only. Reads 8-12 full bodies plus metadata (estimate +40-70K main-context tokens).

mechanisms.name: Period-pinned primary-filing pre-flight
mechanisms.what: For every time period named in the decomposition, the orchestrator searches the vault for the filing that covers that exact period, opens it to confirm the reporting period, and logs any miss as a critical pp-N gap with ready search queries (for example a site:sec.gov 10-Q query), before the critic runs.
mechanisms.why: Targets what the authors call the largest avoidable factual-accuracy failure: paraphrased, rounded or wrong-period numbers. Concrete and cheap, though it only applies to period-pinned queries.
mechanisms.cost: A few vault searches and note reads per time period, plus fetches for misses. Low.

mechanisms.name: Adversarial corpus critic plus targeted fetch wave
mechanisms.what: One Sonnet critic re-reads the 2-3 source notes behind each committed position to check the text supports it, checks whether consensus rests on independent sources, searches the vault for counter-evidence, and outputs 3-8 overturning, strengthening or verification gaps. 2-4 fetchers chase them, and the orchestrator writes confidence changes into comparisons.md.
mechanisms.why: The only pre-draft check of positions against source text, and it corrects before drafting rather than after. Weakened by three things: misreadings have no output channel, 'NOT found' counts as gained confidence, and updates never reach the interim notes that drafters read.
mechanisms.cost: 1 Sonnet critic (estimate 40-80K context) plus 2-4 Sonnet fetchers, each fetching its gaps plus up to 8 chased primaries.

mechanisms.name: Evidence digest of claim quotes grouped by atomic item
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator reads every fetcher-written claims-*.json, keeps high-confidence or empirical/statistical claims (preferring ones with numbers and quotes), caps at 80-120, groups them by atomic item on topic overlap, adds consensus claims and 3-5 contested pairs, and writes bullets of claim, blockquoted quoted_support and source note id.
mechanisms.why: Gives the drafters and the synthesizer (who never reads sources) a compact, cited, quote-bearing index organized around what the prompt asked. But the quotes are unverified at ingest, and the selection is an LLM pass over hundreds of claims with a numeric bias.
mechanisms.cost: The orchestrator reads all claim files (estimate 75-135K tokens if read raw, for 500-900 claims) and writes about 80-120 bullets. Many Read calls or an improvised script.

mechanisms.name: Angle assignment and per-draft curated reading lists
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator assigns three angles (strongest thesis, steelman-contrarian defending the minority view, synthesis reconciler; or breadth, depth, practitioner). Using one quality-ranked search per atomic item, it picks 20-50 note ids per draft. All interim notes and relevant source analyses go in every list; 5-15 angle-specific extras differentiate them.
mechanisms.why: Removes vault-survey loops from the drafters, applies the composite quality ranking (tier, utility, citation authority, PageRank, retraction floor), and gives each draft a slightly different evidence base. Heavy overlap limits real diversity.
mechanisms.cost: Orchestrator: one note list, one ranked search per atomic item, three list files. Moderate main-context load.

mechanisms.name: Three parallel full-length angle drafts (Opus)
mechanisms.what: Three draft-orchestrator subagents (Bash, Read, Write; no fetching, no spawning) each read every listed note in full, in batches of 5-8 via note show, then write a complete draft that honors the required headings, covers every atomic item, commits per section, and meets citation-density and format targets.
mechanisms.why: The contrarian and reconciler angles plausibly surface counterarguments and boundary conditions that a single draft would underplay. But the repo has no ablation; release 0.7.0 removed an earlier three-draft ensemble and V8 restored it on anecdote; and validation is only existence plus more than 1,000 characters.
mechanisms.cost: Highest in the subsystem: 3 Opus sessions, each with an estimated 150-250K peak context (35-50 full notes plus artifacts) and 7-13K output tokens (5,000-10,000 words). 5-15 minutes each in parallel (step 10:183). Truncated Bash output can force extra re-reads.

mechanisms.name: Source-checked conflict verdicts, synthesis plan and outline before writing
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator reads all three drafts. For each substantive contradiction between them it opens both cited sources and writes a verdict. It then writes a plan (core thesis, 3-7 strongest beats with their source draft, per-section commitments, which side to commit to where drafts disagreed, length targets) and a 50-200-word per-H2 outline, and gates on these files existing.
mechanisms.why: Fixes thesis, structure and commitments before the writer starts, and resolves factual conflicts from source text: 'The synthesizer cannot do strategic planning — it can only execute the plan' (11:143). Only cross-draft disagreements are checked, so errors all three drafts share pass.
mechanisms.cost: Orchestrator reads three drafts (estimate 20-40K tokens) plus the conflicting sources, and writes three small files.

mechanisms.name: Fresh-context two-pass synthesizer (Opus, Read+Write only)
mechanisms.what: A new session reads drafts, plan, outline, digest and artifacts and rewrites the report from scratch in one voice, never grafting. Pass 1 runs 15-20% long with full coverage, primers, definitions, tables, numbered headings and dense citations. Pass 2 cuts redundancy, repairs voice breaks, rewrites weak sections, cuts prose (never points) to the hard ceiling, applies calm citation placement and register discipline, and runs a six-item structural checklist.
mechanisms.why: This is where the final prose is made, outside the orchestrator's degraded context. The rules are specific and tied to documented regressions and fixes (CHANGELOG.md:185, 207, 211, 213). A real tool allowlist on Claude Code stops it from re-researching or spawning.
mechanisms.cost: 1 Opus session: estimate 45-75K input and 15-30K output tokens (two full-length files), 5-15 minutes (11:206), plus possibly one more full run for compression.

mechanisms.name: Mechanical length gate, one compression re-spawn, write-once
mechanisms.what: The orchestrator counts words with wc or Python against the profile ceiling. If over, it re-spawns the synthesizer once on its own output to cut to mid-range. Other defects get hand Edits. After step 11 the report changes only through patch hunks. The ship gate later re-checks length within ±20%.
mechanisms.why: Prevents over-long reports and regenerate loops, and is one of the few limits enforced in code. Compressing from the report alone, without the drafts, risks losing points.
mechanisms.cost: One count command; at most one extra Opus synthesizer run.

mechanisms.name: Run-directive shims pasted verbatim into every spawn
mechanisms.what: Step 1 picks a register (teach, survey, analyze, advocate) and an inference depth (surface, standard, deep). levers.py renders research, drafting, critics and polish shims that steps 5, 8, 10 and 11 append verbatim to spawn prompts, overriding defaults such as 'commit, don't hedge'.
mechanisms.why: Adapts posture to the question (teach vs advocate). The changelog reports '+2.5 RACE from register alone' on a test question (CHANGELOG.md:194).
mechanisms.cost: A few hundred tokens per spawn.

mechanisms.name: Per-step skill loading with state kept on disk
mechanisms.what: Each step's procedure is loaded fresh when needed (a Skill call, or a step-file read on Codex), and every step re-reads its inputs from run files, so compaction cannot evict a procedure before it is used.
mechanisms.why: Fixes the documented V7 failure where compaction dropped the corpus critic and the triple draft. It is still only a reminder: no code checks that the steps ran.
mechanisms.cost: One Skill call per step plus re-reading inputs, which duplicates context (interim notes are read in both 5.4 and 6).

mechanisms.name: Untrusted-source fencing of fetched bodies
mechanisms.what: note show wraps web-sourced bodies in untrusted-source tags with a treat-as-data notice. Interim and source-analysis notes pass unwrapped as trusted. Agent prompts carry a policy against obeying fenced text.
mechanisms.why: Prompt-injection safety, not report quality. Fenced text paraphrased into an interim note loses its fence.
mechanisms.cost: Negligible.

weaknesses.issue: Nothing in code checks that steps 5-11 ran
weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/core/runs.py:808-842 checks only critic, patch and polish artifacts and cite-check. Nothing checks draft-{a,b,c}.md, source-tensions.json, evidence-digest.md or the synthesis plan. The locus-coverage and workflow lint rules (src/hyperresearch/cli/lint.py:1005-1095, 1603-1624) sit outside the gate, which folds in only quote-integrity and retracted-citations (runs.py:783-806). The entry skill admits V7 'silently dropped Layer 3.7 (corpus critic), rewrote its todo to replace the triple-draft ensemble with a single draft' (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch.md:309).
weaknesses.impact: A run can skip depth, the critic or the triple draft and still finish 'done'. Users cannot tell a degraded run from a full one.

weaknesses.issue: The final writer works second-hand, and the fidelity check is loose
weaknesses.evidence: The synthesizer reads drafts plus the digest (src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:2183-2210) and is limited to Read and Write (2117). Only contradictions between drafts are source-checked (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-11-synthesize.md:53: 'For each substantive contradiction between drafts'). quote-integrity accepts a span that 'must exist in some vault note body' (src/hyperresearch/cli/lint.py:110-148), and interim notes are indexed vault notes with frontmatter (src/hyperresearch/core/sync.py:48-56, 96-99).
weaknesses.impact: Errors shared by all three drafts, or misquotes that live in an interim note, reach the final report undetected at this stage.

weaknesses.issue: Unbounded full-body reading by each drafter
weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:1969-1970 'You MUST read every one before writing', with 20-50 ids per drafter (src/hyperresearch/core/profiles.py:290). note show returns the whole body with no paging (src/hyperresearch/cli/note.py:219-226). The prompt expects truncation: 'If a batch returns truncated bodies, re-read those IDs individually' (hooks.py:2006-2008).
weaknesses.impact: Very high token cost across three Opus sessions. Long notes can still be cut by the host's Bash output cap when read singly. The 'verification gate' (2023-2028) counts IDs passed, not content seen.

weaknesses.issue: Locus schema drifts between producer, merger and consumer
weaknesses.evidence: The analyst emits 'convergent'|'dialectical' with corpus_evidence and opposing_positions (src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:264-289). The merged loci.json schema has 'dialectical|synthesis|technical' and neither field (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-4-loci-analysis.md:83-102). The step 5 template passes only name, one_line, flavor, budget and rationale (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-5-depth-investigation.md:48-53). The investigator expects 'the full locus object ... corpus_evidence ... opposing_positions' (hooks.py:396-398) and starts from corpus_evidence (425-428).
weaknesses.impact: Investigators can lose their seed notes and the two sides of dialectical loci, then rediscover them or drift. 'synthesis' and 'technical' loci get no posture (hooks.py:405-421 covers only convergent and dialectical).

weaknesses.issue: On Claude Code, depth fetching depends on a subagent spawning subagents (unverified)
weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:348 'tools: Bash, Read, Write, Task' and 443-446 'Do NOT call {hpr_path} fetch directly. Delegate to hyperresearch-fetcher via the Task tool'. The only test is a string check (tests/test_core/test_hooks.py:175-176). For Codex the project says 'You cannot spawn subagents' (src/hyperresearch/core/codex.py:132) and rewrites the rule (171-181).

weaknesses.issue: Source budgets are instruction-only, and fetcher chasing multiplies them
weaknesses.evidence: The brackets allow 15 per top locus across 6 loci, against 'Total source budget for step 5 is 40' (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-4-loci-analysis.md:75-81). The critic has no gap type for misreadings (src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:3313) and must 'NOT re-litigate the investigators' positions' (3338-3340). Every tension named here becomes a subsection in the final report.' No step 10 or 11 prompt requires such a section (grep finds the phrase only in step 7). With prescribed headings, extra H2s are forbidden (src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:2036-2038).

Build the ## Sources list as you go' versus the default wikilink style: 'No separate ## Sources section' (hooks.py:2393) and 'Do NOT add numbered references' (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-11-synthesize.md:192-196).

weaknesses.issue: Strategic decisions are made in the most loaded context
weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-11-synthesize.md:20 'the orchestrator has been running for 30+ minutes and 200K+ tokens of context'; 11:143 'The synthesizer cannot do strategic planning — it can only execute the plan'. Angles, reading lists, conflict verdicts and the core thesis are all written by the orchestrator (steps 10.1-10.2, 11.2-11.4).
weaknesses.impact: The quality of the thesis and the source curation depends on an orchestrator that is likely near or past compaction.

weaknesses.issue: Step 9 runs a mechanical filter by having an LLM read every claim
weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-9-evidence-digest.md:33 'Read all claims files'. The claims CLI filters only by note, tag and limit (src/hyperresearch/cli/claims_cmd.py:77-95). quoted_support is stored unverified (src/hyperresearch/core/claims.py:126-147), yet the digest is described as 'higher-fidelity' primary evidence (9:16).
weaknesses.impact: Large main-context load (estimate 75-135K tokens for 500-900 claims). Unverified quotes enter as primary evidence. The numeric preference (9:35) can starve qualitative, legal or historical questions.

weaknesses.issue: The triple draft is the costliest mechanism, and its value is unmeasured
weaknesses.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:390: release 0.7.0 'replaces the three-parallel-drafts-plus-merger ensemble design' with a pipeline where 'one draft is written from the combined evidence'. V8 restored three drafts citing V7 anecdotes (src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch.md:309; src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-10-triple-draft.md:16). All lists share every interim note and source analysis (10:115-116). Validation threshold is 'under 1000 chars' (10:203).
weaknesses.impact: About three extra full Opus drafts per run, with no evidence in the repo that they beat one well-briefed draft. Shared inputs limit how different the drafts are.

weaknesses.issue: Pressure toward invented precision in interim notes
weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:555-582 'state a specific rule, threshold, percentage, time window, or named mechanism', with fabricated examples such as '(5—8s for typical drivers per Zhang 2022 [N])'. Nothing checks numbers in interim notes, and the report-level numeric-consistency rule is 'Warning severity' only (src/hyperresearch/cli/lint.py, _check_numeric_consistency).
weaknesses.impact: Specific-sounding but weakly sourced thresholds can pass from interim notes into all three drafts and the final report.

weaknesses.evidence: src/hyperresearch/skills/hyperresearch-6-cross-locus-reconcile.md:64 'the insight score suffers'; src/hyperresearch/core/hooks.py:2221-2222 'flat ## Title lists score lower on instruction-following'; hooks.py:2232 sets an 80-150 citation target for argumentative reports; CHANGELOG.md:194 '+2.5 RACE from register alone'.
