ideas_for_vafer: Adopt the four-verdict binding check (supported / partially-supported / unsupported / wrong-source; 'does THIS source say it', not 'is it true') in VAFER's step-6 re-open pass, run by a fresh subagent that sees only the sentence and the cited page text.
Adopt: when a note stores a verbatim quote, check it against the fetched page text at once (exact or whitespace-normalized match). hyperresearch never verifies quoted_support.
Adopt: treat any mismatch in number, unit, date or magnitude as critical, whatever verdict label it gets.
Adopt: make the final check list every critical finding with its resolution (new text, or removed). An empty or pre-created log never counts as resolution.
Adopt a coverage check: have the verifier list factual sentences in key sections that carry no citation. hyperresearch never checks uncited sentences.

Adopt bounded excerpts: give the verifier the stored quote and its surrounding passage, or a targeted re-open, instead of full page bodies. This cuts tokens and avoids false 'unsupported' verdicts caused by truncated output.

Avoid substring auto-passes on numbers or n-grams. If VAFER adds a mechanical pre-check, strip citation markers first, match whole number tokens with units, and use it only to flag pairs, never to skip the reading check.
Avoid silent drops: every [n] in the body must map to a source-list entry, and every entry to a page opened in this run. Unparseable citations must fail loudly, not pass empty.

Adapt independence: a cluster of copies is exactly one voice (sum = 1), and the root is chosen by publication date or primary domain, not fetch order. Keep VAFER's 'copies of one account count once' rule (SKILL.md:55) and add a worked example.

Adapt the fence if VAFER ever wraps page text for subagents: a random tag per run, applied on every path, including quotes passed between agents. Never treat LLM summaries of hostile pages as trusted.
Avoid accepting quotes or support found in LLM-written summaries or notes: a quote must match the cited page's own text.
Avoid making 'remove the quotation marks' an acceptable fix for a failed quote check: require fix-to-verbatim or deletion.

Avoid building PageRank or composite source ranking. In hyperresearch it shifts relevance about 4%, only within the top-N, and its provenance edges point the wrong way; VAFER's primary-record-first rule does more at no cost.
Adapt sentence handling if VAFER ever binds citations mechanically: make it language-aware (Turkish capitals, CJK 。！？, citations after the period), or bind at paragraph level and say so.
Adopt the hostile-input hygiene of hyperresearch's claims ingest (size caps, type coercion, path containment) in any VAFER script that reads agent-written JSON derived from web pages.
Avoid POSIX-only 'VAR=value command' prefixes in prompts that may run under PowerShell, since VAFER targets Codex as well as Claude Code.
If VAFER cites papers, adopt a retraction check that works with any citation style; hyperresearch's covers only wikilink citations of DOI-bearing notes.

key_claims.claim: The mechanical cite-check triage auto-passes wrong numbers. It tests the sentence's numbers as substrings of the cited note's LLM-extracted claims, and those numbers include the citation index itself. Auto-passed pairs are never checked by the LLM. Probe: 'grew 5%' passes against a 25% claim, '[12]' passes because of '2012', and 86% of the example report's pairs carry their own index as a number.

The cite-check part of the ship gate checks only that files exist: the findings file, and a patch log when there are critical findings. The step-14.5 skill pre-creates that log. patch-surgery checks only step 14's log and is not in the gate. Nothing requires step 14.5 to have run at all.

Numbered citations with no Sources entry are dropped silently. A Sources section with a non-standard heading, or with entries not written as '[N] text', yields zero pairs. The skill's empty path then writes [] and the gate passes, so the whole check becomes a vacuous pass.

The independence audit counts a k-copy syndication cluster as 1+(k-1)/k voices, not 1. The root keeps 1.0 and the members get 1/k, which contradicts the 'ONE vote' promise in CHANGELOG.md:241 and the step-3 skill. Two stories syndicated five times each sum to 3.6 and clear the 3.0 consensus bar (probe).

The prompt-injection fence is lexical and covers only some read paths. It is applied only by `note show` (not --raw) and by `search`. It is bypassed by `note show --raw`, by direct Read of note files, by raw claims JSON, and by trusted LLM note types. Homoglyph, zero-width, fullwidth and HTML-entity closers survive unchanged (probe).

Source ranking has little effect and its provenance edges point the wrong way. The quality multiplier (0.5 + quality) is applied after the SQL LIMIT, with a spread of about 1.10-1.20 for non-retracted notes. The --suggested-by breadcrumb is placed on the fetched note, so PageRank rewards the suggester rather than the primaries sources converge on (probe), contrary to the graphrank docstring.

vault.subsystem: Vault, notes, search index, embeddings, links, MCP server and web viewer
vault.summary:
hyperresearch keeps notes as flat markdown files in research/notes/*.md, with YAML frontmatter validated by pydantic. It mirrors them into SQLite: notes, bodies, tags, wiki-links, an FTS5 index, claims, sources, embeddings. Every CLI command and every MCP tool call opens the database, runs schema DDL, then scans the tree and syncs files to the database. Search is FTS5/bm25 with tag, tier and scholarly filters. Embeddings (off by default) add a hybrid ranking mode. Wiki-links and fetch breadcrumbs feed PageRank and a composite quality score. Extras: index pages, an auto-linker, MinHash dedup, a topic tree, batch edits, a 13-tool MCP server and a localhost web viewer.

Within one run, the vault is the shared evidence store. Every step builds its corpus with `--tag <vault_tag>` and reads full source text from it. Across runs it adds almost nothing. Each run mints a fresh unique tag, already-fetched URLs are skipped without the new tag, and final reports are not indexed. The draft-to-evergreen lifecycle is mechanical and the pipeline never runs it.

Costs: about 0.6 s per read call and 0.9 s per write call at 2,000 notes, and full bodies in search JSON. The pipeline's own CLI commands do not use the lifecycle, index pages, embeddings, dedup, topics, MCP or the viewer.

mechanisms.name: Markdown-first flat vault with slug ids
mechanisms.what: Each source or note is research/notes/<id>.md with YAML frontmatter (NoteMeta, about 30 fields, extra keys ignored). The id is the Unicode-aware slugify of the title, capped at 80 chars and 200 bytes. Collision suffixes also skip ids already in the DB. parent is metadata only, never a folder.
mechanisms.why: It gives every later step and subagent durable, re-readable full source text for the run (drafters, critics, cite-check). The storage itself adds no judgment.
mechanisms.cost: Body stored 4 times: .md file plus body, body_plain and the FTS copy. Measured 72 MB SQLite for 21 MB markdown at 2,000 notes. Negligible tokens.

mechanisms.name: Incremental file-to-DB sync on every command
mechanisms.what: rglob over research/**/*.md; skip root staging files, runs/ and files without frontmatter. Compare mtime, then sha256. Upsert notes, tags, aliases, content, FTS and links in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, then re-resolve every NULL link with four UPDATEs, two of them unindexed LOWER() joins. auto_sync discards the error list.
mechanisms.why: Plumbing that keeps the DB in step with files. Its failure modes (silent drops, lock errors) can hurt.
mechanisms.cost: Measured at 2,000 notes: 0.63-0.77 s no-change scan; one-note change 0.70 s with 0 broken links vs 13.8 s with 6,000. Lock held throughout, default 5 s busy timeout (core/db.py:233). 5 of 6 parallel writers failed in the broken-link case; 12 of 12 succeeded in the clean case.

mechanisms.name: FTS5 search with bm25 weights, status multipliers and optional quality re-rank
mechanisms.what: Each query word becomes a quoted prefix term (implicit AND); raw passthrough if the query contains AND/OR/NOT/NEAR. bm25 column weights: title 10, body 1, tags 5, aliases 3. Then evergreen x1.5, deprecated x0.3, stale x0.7, and --ranked multiplies by 0.5+quality. Re-ranking happens after SQL LIMIT/OFFSET.
mechanisms.why: Steps 8, 10 and 13 and agent prompts use it for tag-scoped evidence and gap checks. But one absent keyword returns zero hits (measured), so gap checks can report false absences. Re-ranking only reorders the current page.
mechanisms.cost: Queries are fast. JSON mode auto-includes full bodies at default limit 20 (cli/search.py:177): measured 236,614 bytes vs 22,983 with --no-body. No pipeline call caps it.

mechanisms.name: Tag-scoped corpus assembly (vault_tag per run)
mechanisms.what: Each run mints a unique vault_tag. Fetchers tag notes with it. Every step lists or searches with --tag <vault_tag>, and chapters use <vault_tag>-<ch> tags.
mechanisms.why: Within a run it isolates the corpus and lets each step build reading lists. Across runs it hides earlier sources, which hurts overlapping re-runs.
mechanisms.cost: note list --all -j returns every summary: 793,824 bytes at 2,000 notes. Estimated 50-150 KB per call for a 55-130-note run with multi-paragraph summaries.

mechanisms.name: Structured metadata filters
mechanisms.what: SearchFilters builds SQL for tags (AND), status, type, tier, content_type, dates, path glob, parent, word counts, DOI, venue, min citations, retraction, OA version, and graph filters (linked_from/to, min_inbound, has_backlinks).
mechanisms.why: Tag filtering is load-bearing for corpus scope. Tier and scholarly filters exist, but the pipeline mostly uses --tag only.
mechanisms.cost: Cheap SQL.

mechanisms.name: Untrusted-source fencing on CLI reads
mechanisms.what: note show and search-with-bodies wrap the body of any http(s)-sourced note that is not interim, source-analysis, moc or index. Forged fence tags are neutralized and the URL is escaped. note show also adds a structured oa block for open-access substitutions.
mechanisms.why: It lowers the risk that injected page text steers subagents, and it tells readers when the body is a preprint. MCP and note show --raw bypass it.
mechanisms.cost: About 90 tokens per wrapped body.

mechanisms.name: Wiki-link extraction, resolution and provenance breadcrumbs
mechanisms.what: [[target]] links, extracted after a linear code-strip and heavy junk filtering. Resolution order: exact id, case-insensitive id, alias, title, each LIMIT 1. fetch --suggested-by prepends a 'Suggested by [[src]]' breadcrumb to record citation chains.
mechanisms.why: Provenance edges feed PageRank, quality_score and step 10's --ranked order. Otherwise bookkeeping.
mechanisms.cost: Resolution cost scales with broken links x notes and runs inside the write lock.

mechanisms.name: PageRank centrality and composite quality score
mechanisms.what: Power-iteration PageRank (damping 0.85, max 50 iterations) over all non-stub notes, index pages included, normalized by the max. Quality is a renormalized weighted sum: tier 0.35, utility/18 0.20, authority 0.25, centrality 0.20; retracted floored at 0.05.
mechanisms.why: Called in step 2 (graph rank) and used by step 10 search --ranked. It only reorders hits bm25 already selected. Centrality is vault-wide and gets distorted by index pages (recency, self-reinforcing most-linked).
mechanisms.cost: Pure Python and small. Requires graph rank and sources score calls.

mechanisms.name: Per-source LLM curation by fetcher subagents
mechanisms.what: For each URL: sources check, fetch, note show (full body), relevance/junk/duplicate verdict (deprecate via note update), summary sized to source density, tags, claims JSON with verbatim quoted_support.
mechanisms.why: Summaries, deprecations and quoted claims are what downstream digest, drafting and cite-check consume.
mechanisms.cost: About 5 CLI calls per source, about 3-5 s local overhead per source (estimate from measured parts), plus full body tokens into the fetcher context.

mechanisms.name: URL-level fetch dedup (sources table)
mechanisms.what: Exact-URL lookup before fetching; an orphaned row (note deleted) counts as not fetched on the fetch path. A duplicate gives a DUPLICATE_URL error or a breadcrumb append, and never adds the caller's tag. fetch-batch reports only a skipped count.
mechanisms.why: It saves a refetch, but across runs it hides the existing note from the new run's tag-scoped corpus, which is negative for reuse.
mechanisms.cost: One sources check CLI call per URL (about 0.6 s each).

mechanisms.name: Auto-linker
mechanisms.what: Vocabulary is every title of 15+ characters plus every note id regardless of length. Each entry is regex-searched in each target note, then '## Related' with [[ids]] is appended to the file on disk.
mechanisms.where: core/linker.py:12-138; called by cli/fetch_batch.py:339-348 and cli/link.py:57
mechanisms.why: Measured false positives ([[python]], [[wikipedia]] from incidental mentions). It mutates fetched text and injects fake provenance into PageRank.
mechanisms.cost: O(notes x vocab) regex scans, then a re-sync.

mechanisms.name: Auto-generated index pages
mechanisms.what: Deletes all research/index/*.md, then writes master, tags, per-tag (3+ notes), recent, orphans, stats, raw-pending, per-month, stale and most-linked pages as type=index notes.
mechanisms.why: The pipeline never reads them and search excludes type=index. They distort PageRank. Measured crash on a tag containing '/'.
mechanisms.cost: About 10+ page rewrites plus a sync per rebuild.

mechanisms.name: Embeddings and hybrid search
mechanisms.what: Optional Voyage or OpenAI vectors of title, summary and the first 1,500 body chars. Freshness stamp is model@content_hash. Brute-force Python cosine, fused with FTS by reciprocal rank fusion (k=60).
mechanisms.why: Provider is 'none' by default and the pipeline never calls embed sync or --semantic.
mechanisms.cost: Paid API calls when enabled. Any frontmatter edit re-embeds the note. Python cosine over all vectors per query.

mechanisms.name: Curation lifecycle (status, repair promotion, enrich)
mechanisms.what: draft to review needs 50+ words, a summary and a tag; review to evergreen needs 100+ words and any link. auto_tag scores a tag whenever any single word of it appears in the body; auto_summary takes the first line of 25+ chars. expires and reviewed exist but nothing sets them.
mechanisms.why: No pipeline step runs repair; the ritual is a CLAUDE.md instruction only. Promotion rules are mechanical, yet evergreen gets a 1.5x search boost. auto_tag leaks other runs' tags (measured).
mechanisms.cost: When run: rewrites many files and triggers re-syncs; per-note try/except swallows failures.

mechanisms.name: MCP server (13 tools)
mechanisms.what: FastMCP stdio server. search_notes, read_note, read_many, list_notes, get_backlinks, get_hubs, vault_status, lint_vault, check_source, list_sources, fetch_url, create_note, update_note. Each tool call runs auto_sync.
mechanisms.why: Optional extra for Claude Desktop/Cursor. Not registered by install and not used by the pipeline.
mechanisms.cost: An auto_sync scan per call. search_notes returns full raw bodies (default limit 10). A slow fetch_url blocks the loop.

mechanisms.name: Local web viewer
mechanisms.what: stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1:8080 serving note pages with backlinks, tags, FTS search (limit 50) and a canvas force-directed graph from /api/graph. One SQLite connection per request, no sync.
mechanisms.why: For humans browsing only.
mechanisms.cost: No pipeline cost. The graph layout is O(n^2) per tick in the browser.

mechanisms.name: Agent-docs injection at vault init
mechanisms.what: Writes or updates a marked hyperresearch block in CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md for Codex). The block holds CLI path, pipeline entry, fetch rules, OA disclosure rules, search commands, untrusted policy and the curate-after-every-session ritual.

ideas_for_vafer: Adopt: question-level reuse via INDEX.md (already planned). When a URL or fact was used before, copy its saved quote, URL and access date into the current run's notes instead of skipping it. Never let a 'seen before' check hide evidence.
Avoid: hyperresearch's per-run unique tag plus URL dedup with no retagging, which makes overlapping re-runs see fewer sources.
Adopt: make the final report itself findable (INDEX line plus plain grep). Never make indexing depend on frontmatter that the writing step is told to omit.
Avoid: a shared SQLite index written by parallel researchers. VAFER's per-researcher notes/<id>.md files cannot hit lock contention; keep it that way.
Adopt: search helpers return paths and short snippets only, never full bodies, and stay well under the host's tool-output cap.
Adapt: use any-term matching (several rg -i -e patterns) for 'do we already have evidence on X' checks, and log zero-hit queries as 'not found with these queries', never as 'no evidence'.
Adopt: treat saved research and quoted page text as data on every read path, including reuse. hyperresearch fences the CLI only and leaves MCP raw.
Adopt: carry an access date and a volatility class per saved fact and re-check volatile ones on reuse. hyperresearch has expires/reviewed fields nothing sets.
Avoid: mechanical quality labels (word count plus any link = 'evergreen') that then boost ranking. If VAFER marks quality, tie it to verification ('quote re-checked on date X').
Avoid: automatic substring auto-linking and single-word auto-tagging. They fabricate provenance and leak notes across runs.
Adapt: keep the cited passage (30 words or fewer) with URL and date as the unit of storage. Optionally save raw text only for pages behind headline facts, so the final re-check survives link rot.
Adopt: exclude rejected or off-topic sources by construction (separate section or file), not by an instruction to skip a status value.
Avoid: destructive regeneration. Never delete derived files before the inputs validate (hyperresearch deletes all index pages, then crashes on one tag).
Avoid: a large always-loaded instructions block. hyperresearch's CLAUDE.md block costs about 15.5k chars per session in the vault folder.
Adopt: surface every write or parse failure to the agent. hyperresearch's auto_sync discards errors, so notes vanish silently.
Adapt: if VAFER ever caches pages, key the cache by normalized URL and report cache hits with their saved location. hyperresearch's fetch-batch reports only a skipped count.

missed: Fetchers search too, and they add to the queue. The fetcher prompt makes Phase 2 mandatory ('This phase is NON-OPTIONAL', core/hooks.py:3152-3158): each fetcher chases 3-8 more sources (core/profiles.py:272-273) and uses WebSearch to find them (core/hooks.py:3181). This contradicts the step-2 spawn prompt, 'you fetch ONLY the URLs in your batch. Do not search for additional URLs' (skills/hyperresearch-2-width-sweep.md:144-146) and 'No fetcher searches for new URLs' (:157). Waves 2 and 3 add 3-5 and 2-3 more fetchers (core/profiles.py:266-267).

'Blocked pages are queued' needs limits. Hard fetch exceptions are never queued (cli/fetch.py:352-361), even though 'fetch_failed' is a defined reason (core/escalation.py:22). fetch-batch never escalates at all (cli/fetch_batch.py:169-180). Scored URLs below utility 8.0 are dropped, and the queue stops at 25 per run (core/config.py:96-100, core/escalation.py:76-85). One browser-fetcher drains up to 10 per spawn (hyperresearch-2-width-sweep.md:255,273), and Codex never drains (:249-254). The lane is a Sonnet agent driving Chrome; humans step in only for CAPTCHA, login or 2FA (core/hooks.py:3371-3385).

The junk gate also rejects by substring. Any title, or the first 2000 body characters, containing 'cloudflare', 'access denied', 'ray id', 'captcha', 'an error occurred', 'the page you requested' and similar phrases is rejected (web/base.py:119-138). Running the real code rejected 'Cloudflare Q3 2024 earnings' and 'Access denied: the politics of ...' as bot pages, and 'An error occurred in the Fed model' as an error page. Error pages are dropped, not escalated (cli/fetch.py:394-399).

The SSRF gate is only partial on the browser lane. It checks the entry URL and the final URL, so intermediate redirects and subresource requests go unchecked; the code itself says 'blind SSRF survives' (web/crawl4ai_provider.py:200-209). The final-URL check is skipped when the host is unchanged (:214-219). The visible/profile lane always ignores TLS errors (:347-356). By contrast, the builtin, PDF and OA lanes re-check every redirect hop through safe_get (web/safe_http.py:11,289-353).

Scholarly search is wired unevenly. The step-2 skill says to query 'Semantic Scholar / arXiv / OpenAlex / PubMed' (hyperresearch-2-width-sweep.md:45,95) and never names `hpr scholar search`, whose registry contains none of Semantic Scholar, arXiv or PubMed (scholar/registry.py:22-31). The contact email is split in two: `[scholar] contact_email` drives Unpaywall (core/config.py:183), while the HYPERRESEARCH_CONTACT_EMAIL environment variable drives EDGAR and the OpenAlex/Crossref polite pool (scholar/base.py:69-72). Europe PMC full-text requests also send a hard-coded 'mailto:research@example.com' (core/oa.py:537).

missed: citation_style is ignored by the gate, so a documented 'none'-style run can never ship. Skipping steps 2–11, 13 or 16 (loci, depth, comparisons, digest, triple draft, synthesis) does not fail it. Cite-check is weaker still. 14.5 is not a profile step, since steps are ints 1–16 (core/profiles.py:123, 234-244), so resume never schedules it. Its check runs only if the manifest records 14.5 as done (runs.py:824), and 'resolved' just means cite-check-patch-log.json exists (runs.py:834-838).

Any 'retract' within 200 characters of the link also waives the check (lint.py:218-220).

In non-interactive Claude Code runs, the width-sweep skill says to `run block <tag> --on human-challenges` and CONTINUE the pipeline (skills/hyperresearch-2-width-sweep.md:282). But set_step refuses every `--status done` while the run is blocked on a non-count reason: 'this block cannot be cleared with --force' (core/runs.py:259-269). The manifest therefore stops recording progress, and 14.5 can't be recorded as done, so its gate check is skipped. Only `run resume` gets out, and it flips any block (verify, budget, human-challenges) or a failed run back to running (cli/run_cmd.py:207-208).

A second code-level enforcer is missing from the summary: the Codex-only Stop hook `hpr run stop-gate` (cli/run_cmd.py:249-294; core/codex.py:337-386). It refuses to end a Codex session while the newest run is 'running', was touched in the last 6 hours and has a next step. It is soft: it lets the stop through on the second attempt (stop_hook_active, run_cmd.py:276), never fires for blocked runs (codex.py:361) and is off when HYPERRESEARCH_STOP_GATE=0 (run_cmd.py:265). So 'only verify_run binds' holds only for quality.

In graphrank.py:40-57 rank flows from source to target (`incoming[dst].append(src)`), so the suggester gains rank and the chased primary gains only out-links. graphrank.py:4-8 states the opposite meaning. config.py:115-118 gives w_centrality 0.20 of 1.00, but quality.py:3-12 and 37-53 renormalize over whichever components are present. `graph rank` runs at width-sweep.md:232 and is re-run after the browser-lane drain (:269, :283, Claude Code branch only). No later step runs it.
verdicts.correction: The mechanism is right, and it applies vault-wide because graphrank.py:74-93 has no tag filter. The 20% is a nominal weight. Renormalization raises centrality's effective share whenever components are missing: for a note with no DOI it is 0.20/0.75, about 27%. Centrality is computed at step 2.7, recomputed once more after the step-2.8 browser drain, and never after step 2.

verdicts.evidence: hooks.py:3083-3087: '1. Check if it's already fetched ... 2. If not already fetched, fetch it: ... fetch "<url>" --tag <topic>'. fetch.py:254-296: for an existing URL the --tag values are never applied; the command either appends a body breadcrumb (fetch.py:36-84) or exits with 'DUPLICATE_URL'. sources.py:81-86 is an exact-URL lookup; it even reports exists:true for orphaned rows whose note_id is NULL. note.py:347-349 filters on the exact tag. Run-scoped selection uses `--tag <vault_tag>` at width-sweep.md:183, loci-analysis.md:28, triple-draft.md:33/62/110 and runs.py:327-349. The only retag instruction is '--add-tag <specific-tag>' for newly fetched content (hooks.py:3104). This contradicts README.md:59: 'your next session reuses before it fetches anything new'.
verdicts.correction: No correction needed. No prompt or code path adds the run tag to a pre-existing note; a model could add one on its own, but nothing tells it to.

verdicts.evidence: The lead-side load is real. width-sweep.md:97 (all planned searches), :192 (gap searches), :111 (URL scoring), and :210 plus contradiction-graph.md:33 (all claims read twice). hooks.py:3206 sends every summary back to the lead. synthesize.md:20 itself says the orchestrator has reached '200K+ tokens of context'. But the per-source work runs in fetchers: fetching, full reads, summaries, claim extraction and 3–8 chases each (hooks.py:3080-3200). Loci analysts read the corpus in step 4 (loci-analysis.md:34). Fetchers also run WebSearch (hooks.py:3181). Step 3 ignores code that already exists: claims are ingested at width-sweep.md:229, and core/claims.py:342-399 `group_by_target` groups claims by stance_target across sources.
verdicts.correction: Overstated. The lead holds the corpus-level work, not the bulk of it. It runs the planned and gap searches, scores the candidate URLs (full tier only), receives every fetcher summary, and reads all claims files twice (full tier only). The context cost is real, and step 3 could use the ingested claims table (`claims targets`) instead of reloading the raw files.

verdicts.evidence: Confirmed for steps 2-4. runs.py:810-842 checks artifacts only for steps 12/14, 15 and a self-reported 14.5. Nothing checks search-plan.md, coverage-gaps.md, redundancy-audit.md, contradiction-graph.json, consensus-claims.json or loci.json (grep finds these names only in prompts, lint.py and archive.py), and nothing checks coverage-matrix.md. However, the gate does read step 1's prompt-decomposition.json (runs.py:675-684) and checks that step 1's shim files exist (runs.py:691-703). Escape clauses: width-sweep.md:341 'proceed anyway'; contradiction-graph.md:27 'skip this step entirely'; loci-analysis.md:59 'proceed with the successful outputs' and :114 the skip_loci exemption. decompose.md:179 has none. The step-15 `locus-coverage` lint reads loci.json but is advisory ('do not re-run, just note in the run log', polish.md:136).
verdicts.correction: Partly overstated. The step 2-4 rules and step 1's coverage matrix are prompt-only, and the gate checks none of their artifacts. The gate does use step 1's decomposition (headings, format, tier) and checks step 1's shim files. Not every rule has an escape hatch: the zero-gap and adversarial rules have none and are simply unchecked.

missed: Step 1's self-declared pipeline_tier decides what the ship gate checks. `_required_step_ids` prefers it over the manifest profile (runs.py:627-646), so declaring 'light' drops the critic-findings and patch-log requirements (runs.py:810-817), and an unknown value silently falls back to the manifest steps (runs.py:645). The same value routes `run resume` (runs.py:516-525), and nothing validates it.

Code tiers cannot hold half-steps. Profile.steps is a tuple of integers 1–16 (profiles.py:123, 240, 256), so 14.5 and 1.5 never appear among resume's remaining steps (runs.py:483-490), and `run resume` and the Codex stop gate go from step 14 straight to 15. The gate checks cite-check output only when the model itself recorded 14.5 as done (runs.py:824), so a skipped 14.5 passes silently.

The gate does not require prompt-decomposition.json. If the file is missing, the heading list is empty and passes, and the length and shim checks are skipped (runs.py:675-705, 732). The length check is also skipped for any response_format that is not a word_targets key (runs.py:705). Headings are matched as plain substrings anywhere in the report (runs.py:732), not as H2 lines in order as step 1 demands (decompose.md:45), so '### 1. X' satisfies '## 1. X'.

Step 1 offers citation_style 'none' (decompose.md:139), but the gate's citation-density check ignores citation_style and requires at least 9 citations per 1000 words (runs.py:747-770; profiles.py:298). A 'none' run can never pass `run finish`.

Step 1 is the only step with no template variables. Its response-format word bands are hard-coded to the full gear's values (decompose.md:123-125: 2000–5000 and 5000–10000 words), while drafting and the gate use the gear's word_targets (triple-draft.md:48-50; runs.py:705-731). On premier (profiles.py:364: 3000–8000 and 8000–16000), step 1's guidance contradicts what the gate measures.
